issues.legal_issue: A legal representative substituted for a deceased defendant may raise pleas available to the deceased, except pleas personal to the deceased.
material_facts: The claimant was brought into the suit as the legal representative of a deceased defendant and sought to file an additional written statement based on a will.
The deceased defendant had a life interest under the will, and the claimant's asserted interest was also said to arise under that will.
issues.conclusion: A legal representative may raise all pleas the deceased defendant had or could have raised, except pleas personal to the deceased.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXII Rule 4(2) permits a legal representative to raise pleas available to the deceased defendant, except those personal to the deceased. The Court relied on Bal Kishan v. Om Parkash, AIR 1986 SC 1952, and Jagdish Chander Chatterjee v. Sri Kishan, 1973 (1) SCR 850.

predicates.civil_suit_with_substituted_representati: A defendant in a civil suit dies and another person is substituted to represent that defendant's estate.
predicates.plea_available_to_deceased: The substituted representative seeks to raise a plea that the deceased defendant had or could have raised.
predicates.plea_not_personal_to_deceased: The plea does not depend on a right or defence personal to the deceased defendant.

issues.definition: When a person is substituted for a deceased defendant in a civil suit, that person may raise a plea available to the deceased if the plea is not personal to the deceased.

issues.legal_issue: A legal representative cannot assert a title independent of the deceased defendant's title solely in the representative capacity, but may pursue that title after personal joinder or in a separate suit.
material_facts: The claimant asserted a right to the property under the will that was independent of the deceased defendant's life interest.
She sought to assert that right through an additional written statement while acting as the deceased defendant's legal representative.
The Court left the claimant's independent title to be considered in a later proceeding and upheld the refusal to permit her to assert it solely as legal representative.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could assert her independent title by being impleaded in her personal capacity or by bringing a separate suit, but could not assert it solely as the deceased defendant's legal representative.
issues.legal_principle: Order I Rule 10 permits a person asserting an independent interest to be joined in that person's own capacity. The Court relied on Jagdish Chander Chatterjee v. Sri Kishan, 1973 (1) SCR 850, which recognizes that legal representatives may also set up their own independent title if impleaded in their personal capacity, avoiding the need for a separate suit.

predicates.civil_suit_with_substituted_representati: A defendant in a civil suit dies and another person is substituted to represent that defendant's estate.
predicates.representative_asserts_title_independent: The substituted representative seeks to claim a property interest that does not derive from the deceased defendant's interest.

issues.definition: If a substituted representative in a civil suit asserts a property title independent of the deceased defendant's title, that claim requires the representative to be joined personally or to bring a separate suit.
